steps.title: Capture Confocal Images
steps.instruction: Capture images of the plate at 24, 48, and 72 hours post transfection (hpt) using an LSM 710 confocal microscope.

substeps.instruction: Equip the microscope with a plate adapter (Universal mounting frame K-X, Zeiss 451353-0000-0000) and use the 10x objective.
Take a series of non-overlapping adjacent images in the center of the plate to minimize shadows from plate walls.
Overlay fluorescence and brightfield images.
Add additional excitatory channels if necessary to distinguish fluorescent from autofluorescent emissions.
Save images in folders named by the time point (e.g., '6-w.plate.images.48hpt').

steps.title: Standardize and Export Images in Zen Lite
steps.instruction: Use Zen Lite (v 2.6) to isolate the GFP fluorescent channel and standardize brightness across all images.

substeps.instruction: Open files in 'Camera' mode.
Set the green channel histogram from the default 255 to 50.
Save modified images in binary format (.czi) in a new folder.
Select 'Processing' -> 'Batch' mode and select all .czi files.

Export files as TIFF with the following settings: Convert to 8 bit, Compression 'None', Resize 100%, 'Apply Display Settings and Channel Color' checked, 'Individual Channels Image' selected, and 'Define Subset' set to Ch1-T2 (deselect Ch2-T1 and T PMT-T1).
Use 'Copy Parameters' and 'Paste Parameters' to ensure identical export settings for all files.

steps.title: Convert Images in Adobe Photoshop
steps.instruction: Process the exported .tiff images to create high-contrast black and white inverted images.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Image' -> 'Adjustments' -> 'Black and White' and set green to 300%.
Go to 'Image' -> 'Mode' -> 'Grayscale'.
Select 'Flatten' and 'Discard' when prompted about layer loss.
Go to 'Image' -> 'Adjustments' -> 'Invert'.
Export the final result as a .tiff file.
Optional: Create Photoshop 'Actions' or scripts to execute these steps in batch.

steps.title: Quantify Cells in ImageJ (Fiji)
steps.instruction: Import the processed .tiff images into ImageJ to algorithmically count fluorescent cells.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Analyze' -> 'Analyze Particles'.
Empirically adjust size and circularity settings to ensure the majority of fluorescent cells are properly labeled.
Apply the same settings across all images and time points to maintain relative count accuracy.
Record the resulting counts in a text file or spreadsheet.
Optional: Save settings as a 'Macro' to perform batch processing.
